question_verdicts.reason: This is the page's 'P1 asks' item for R1 (the R1 row at Research.md:279; categories.json p1_asks R1). IOBoard.md:221 and hardware/STATUS.md:32 state no deadline. IOBoard.md:162-163 and docs/Safety.md:51 say nothing removes the outputs when the coprocessor freezes and the panel beats, so the monostable's 200 ms does not apply.

It carries marking 39, which is correctly an assumption. IOBoard.md:181 and main.c:1096-1098 name the console print as a second stall. One caveat for the owner: pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb.c:120-121 (read 2026-09-28T10:40:17Z) measures PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US (500,000 us, stdio_usb.h:31-33) from the last time the host accepted data. A host that takes a few bytes within every 500 ms can therefore hold one print longer than 500 ms. 'Up to 500 ms a write' is the bound with no progress, not the per-print maximum.

It carries marking 28, which is correctly an assumption: docs/DShot.md:224 states 'a percent or two' with no source. The decoder's tested 5 % (test_dshot_telem.c:197-217) less that figure is the margin R1 states the crystal against (IOBoard.md:111).

The R1 row checks 'the watchdog timeout' against two bounds. IOBoard.md:221 and hardware/STATUS.md:32 state that no timeout exists, and no watchdog call appears under firmware/iomcu/. Without a value, R1 can report only the window between the stall and the deadline. The page names only the deadline as P1-asked, so the timeout is a missing value too.

IOBoard.md:111 says the crystal's tolerance is not stated, and the R1 row asks R1 to state it. Build 2025-07-29 (read 10:38:05Z) gives Table 597 as ±30 ppm tolerance, ±30 ppm stability and ±5 ppm first-year aging for the ABM8-272-T3. Section 8.1.2.3 reads 'tolerate up to 1000ppm variation in the XOSC frequency'. The figures in the question match.

Table 597 gives CL 10 pF, ESR at most 50 Ohm, C0 at most 3.0 pF, and drive level 10 uW typical and 200 uW maximum. Section 8.2.1.1 says the crystal and damping resistor are 'tuned for 3.3V operation' and 'Any changes to crystal parameters risk instability'. Neither page states these values.

A grep of IOBoard.md, Research.md and hardware/STATUS.md finds no operating temperature range for the board. The only range is the interlock's 0 to 50 °C (IOBoard.md:184, :220). Table 1435 gives the RP2350 -40 to 85 °C ambient. Crystal stability, inductor saturation and protection ratings all depend on the range. It applies to every R1 function, not only the crystal.

Section 6.3.8.2 of build 2025-07-29 (read 10:38:05Z) gives 3.3 uH ±20 %, at most 250 mOhm DC resistance, at least 1.5 A saturation current, fully shielded, polarity-marked, and recommends the AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T. Section 6.3.8.3 asks for low roll-off. IOBoard.md:110 states none of these.

IOBoard.md:118 and :536 put the USB protection in R1 with no level. Table 1434 gives only component-handling figures: 2 kV HBM, 4 kV HBM on FT pins, and 500 V CDM. USB_DP and USB_DM are not FT. P2 needs a system-level target.

IOBoard.md:370 says it is not stated whether the charger's USB-C input is the RP2354B's port. :384 says it is not stated whether that port powers the logic. :140 says the connector type is not stated. F8 fixes 3 A at 5 V for the charger's USB-C. Each of these sets the VBUS rating and the lines the protection covers.

Section 12.7.1 gives a Full Speed device (12 Mb/s), and Table 1431 requires 27 Ohm series resistors. No page states a capacitance limit for a clamp on D+ and D-, so P2 has no figure to drop a part on.

added.question: What highest voltage, in V, may the USB protection let reach USB_DP and USB_DM (QFN-80 pins 67 and 66)? Give the clamping voltage at the ESD level asked in the ESD question, and the highest steady voltage those pins may see.
added.why: The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) types USB_DP and USB_DM as USB IO on USB_OTP_VDD (Tables 1426 and 1431). Its absolute maximum ratings (Table 1433) give a Voltage at IO for Standard and FT pins only. Table 1437 (USB IO) gives no input maximum. Neither page states a limit, so P2 cannot compare a clamp's clamping voltage with the rating of the pins it protects.
added.for_quantity: highest voltage at USB_DP and USB_DM behind the USB protection

added.question: Which connector type does the RP2354B's USB port use: USB Type-C or another type the owner names? How many lines must the protection cover: VBUS, D+ and D-, plus CC1 and CC2 on USB Type-C?
added.why: IOBoard.md:140 says the USB connector type is not stated and leaves connectors to round 2, while IOBoard.md:118 and :536 put the port's protection in round 1 (R1). P1's VBUS question settles only whether the port shares the charger's USB-C connector (IOBoard.md:370). If it does not, the connector and so the lines to clamp stay open. A Type-C receptacle adds CC1 and CC2 to the lines. P2 cannot choose a protection array's channel count or voltage rating per line without it.
added.for_quantity: USB connector type and number of protected lines

added.question: Must the core regulator inductor be fully shielded and marked for polarity (yes or no for each), as section 6.3.8.2 of the RP2350 datasheet requires?
added.why: Section 6.3.8.2 (build 2025-07-29, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) says 'L must be fully shielded' and 'The inductor must be marked for polarity'. Section 6.3.8.3 says field orientation affects the regulator's control loop and output voltage. P1's inductor question asks inductance, saturation current and DC resistance only. IOBoard.md:110 states neither shielding nor polarity marking, so P2 would keep an unmarked or unshielded inductor that meets the three figures.
added.for_quantity: core regulator inductor shielding and polarity marking

added.question: What highest shunt capacitance C0, in pF, and which cut and mode (fundamental AT-cut or another) must the 12 MHz crystal meet?
added.why: Table 597 of the RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) gives the ABM8-272-T3 a C0 of at most 3.0 pF and Fundamental-AT operation. Section 8.2.1.1 says 'Any changes to crystal parameters risk instability'. P1's crystal question asks load capacitance, ESR and drive level only. IOBoard.md:110 states neither C0 nor the mode, so P2 cannot drop a crystal on them.
added.for_quantity: 12 MHz crystal shunt capacitance C0 and mode
